spot: Russia has released 74-year-old American citizen Stephen Hubbard after more than four years in custody, U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff confirmed Wednesday following meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg.
content_html:
Key Developments

U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff confirmed the release of Stephen Hubbard on Wednesday during high-level diplomatic talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg. Russian state media, citing Putin, reported that Hubbard was transferred to St. Petersburg's Pulkovo Airport following the agreement.

Video footage from the St. Petersburg meeting showed Witkoff formally expressing gratitude to the Russian leader, noting that President Donald Trump and the nation sent their thanks for allowing Hubbard to return home to his family. The talks in Russia, which included Witkoff and other senior Trump administration officials, primarily focused on the ongoing war in Ukraine alongside other bilateral matters.

Hubbard, a 74-year-old native of Michigan, had been imprisoned in Russia for more than four years after authorities accused him of fighting on behalf of Ukraine. Currently in poor health, Hubbard is expected to be transported directly to Texas to receive medical treatment at a military hospital.

President Trump stated on Truth Social that Hubbard was freed following a direct personal appeal made during a telephone conversation with Putin last week. Trump emphasized that no prisoner exchange was required to secure Hubbard's freedom, describing the unconditional release as unprecedented. However, the president also noted that the release would not have occurred had the administration not moved to block new, severe sanctions against Russia from taking effect late last week—a decision that drew praise from Putin while facing severe criticism from members of the U.S. Congress.

Key Takeaways

  • Direct Diplomatic Intervention: U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff confirmed Stephen Hubbard's release during face-to-face discussions with Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg.
  • No Prisoner Swap: The White House stated that Russia agreed to release Hubbard without demanding a reciprocal prisoner exchange, shortly after the U.S. waived pending sanctions.
  • Medical Repatriation: Hubbard, who faces deteriorating health after over four years of detention, is scheduled to fly to a military medical facility in Texas.

Why It Matters

Hubbard's release resolves the case of the last U.S. citizen in Russia who had been formally designated as wrongfully detained by the U.S. State Department. While his release marks a significant diplomatic breakthrough amid frosty Washington-Moscow relations, roughly 10 other Americans and dual nationals remain incarcerated in Russian detention facilities.
